{{nihongo|'''Yoshida Shrine'''|吉田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

'''Yoshida Shrine'' (Yoshida Shrine) is located in {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|Q83273|qid=Q83273}}{{ill|Mito, Ibaraki|Q204249|qid=Q204249}} Miyauchi Town. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinai}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), {{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}}, {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=old company rank}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=prefectural company}}.

=== Overview ===
It is located on top of Mt. Asahi, a small hill in the southern part of central Mito city. Its founding tells of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nippon Takeru}}'s involvement in the eastern expedition. Because it enshrines the god of war, Japan Takeru, it is a shrine that has long been highly revered by the Imperial Court during the {{ill|Emishi|Q932574|qid=Q932574}} conquest process. Although the shrine building was burnt down in the war, a place related to Nihon Takeru still remains within the precincts as ``Mt. Sankaku.''

=== Enshrined God ===
The enshrined deity is one of the following<ref name="Yoshisho">Shrine Historysho. </ref>.
* '''{{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nippon Takeru}}''' (Yamato Takeru Mikoto)
*: The 12th {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} prince and father of the 14th {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}. According to "{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}" and "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}," he subjugated the powerful clans of Kyushu and eastern regions on the orders of Emperor Keiko.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
According to ``Joyo Shikinai Chinza Honki'' and ``Hitachi Twenty-eight Shrine Considerations,'' it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nippon Takeru}} rested his soldiers at this place (Mt. Asahi/Mt. Misumi) during his eastern expedition, and the shrine was built in honor of this {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1976}}. The date of its establishment is unknown, but according to ancient documents in the possession of Yoshida Shrine, it was enshrined in {{ill|Shōan|Q1327427|qid=Q1327427}}4 ({{ill|1301|Q5610|qid=Q5610}}). There is a note stating that more than 800 years have passed {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1976}}[http://www.yoshidajinja.jp/hist.html]. The regular autumn festival held on October 19 and 20, 1985 was held as a celebration of the 1500th anniversary of the founding of the company.<ref>Iharaki Shimbun, morning edition of October 21, 1985. </ref>. The location of the shrine's resting place is still told today in a corner of the temple grounds.

Concerning this tradition, there is a theory that the connection to Nihon Takeru dates back to the early {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, since there is no story about Nippon Takeru in Naga District in ``{{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}}'' {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.

The reason why it was ranked 3rd in Hitachi Province and 1st in Naka District (Naka District) is said to be due to its relationship with Japan Takeru, the enshrined god of war, and the Ezo conquest, as well as its relationship with the decline of the Ujibe clan in Naga District, which was dominant in the west of Mito.{{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Taira)|1982}}In the Middle Ages, ``Yoshida County'' was separated from Naga County as the {{ill|Kamigun|ja|神郡|zh|神郡|qid=Q11590937}} of Yoshida Shrine, but the territory of Yoshida Shrine was 158 towns, covering half of Yoshida County {{Sfn|Yoshida County (Taira)|1982}}. From then on, this shrine territory strengthened its character as a manor, and was also called ``Yoshida Manor'' {{Sfn|Yoshida District (Taira)|1982}}. In addition, we call Yakuo-in Temple {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}, and it is said that the shrine had 6-ken and 3-ken corridors, torii gates, and tamagaki, as well as many attached buildings and subsidiary shrines {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Taira)|1982}}, and that the shrine reached the rank of Shoichii {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1976}}. === Shinto priest ===
Yoshida Shrine's social affairs are said to have been handled by ``Kimikoji'' in ancient times {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Taira)|1982}}. The origin and personality of the Yoshimi-kou clan are not clear, but it is said that he belonged to the Emishi tribe in the early Nara period, and there is also a theory that points to a deep relationship with the Emishi {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. After that, Mr. Yoshimiko was appointed to the Central Government during the {{ill|Chōshō|Q1194264|qid=Q1194264}} years ({{ill|1132|Q19582|qid=Q19582}}-{{ill|1135|Q19594|qid=Q19594}}). {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Taira)|1982}}{{Sfn|Yoshida District (Taira)|1982}} who donated a social affairs position (Ryoke position) to the family'''{{ill|Ozuki clan|Q11462133|qid=Q11462133}}'''. This donation is said to have been made to protect the shrine's territory from the interference of local government officials and the invasion of local clans {{Sfn|Yoshida District (Taira)|1982}}. 

Through subsequent changes, there were five former shrine families (the Tadokoro clan, the Akutsu clan, the Sakaki clan, the Watanabe clan, and the Inoue clan) before the Meiji period. After the Shake system was abolished by the Constitution of the Empire of Japan, the Tadokoro clan was in charge until the middle of the Meiji period, and the Akutsu clan thereafter. After the enactment of the Religious Corporations Law after the war, the Akutsu clan was in charge until the early Heisei period after passing through several Shinto priests, and the Tadokoro clan is currently in charge.

=== Precincts ===
The main shrine has {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545}} copper plate roofing, and the worship hall and the shrine have {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}} copper plate roofing, both of which were rebuilt after the war {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1976}}.

On the approach to the shrine, there is a place consecrated as the ``Asahi Sankakuyama Ruins'' where the enshrined deity Nihon Takeru rested {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1976}}. This triangular mountain is said to be the site of the main shrine and rituals {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.

=== Betsugu ===
[[File:Kasahara-koyasu-jinja haiden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|<center>Kasahara Yasu Shrine (Kasahara Town)</center>]]
[[File:Sakado-jinja (Mito) haiden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|<center>Sakamon Shrine (Sakamon Town)</center>]]
"Shuhachisha Ryakuenshi" describes Kasahara Daimyojin and Sakamon Daimyojin as separate shrines.

; Kasahara Yasu Shrine (Kasahara Daimyojin)
:* Enshrinement location: Ichiban, Kasahara-cho, Mito City ({{Coord|36|21|5.17|N|140|27|18.13|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Bekku: Kasaharayasu Shrine}})
:* Deities enshrined: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=younger brother Tachibanahime}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konohanasakuyahime}}: A separate shrine of Yoshida Shrine and one of the seven shrines in Mito. During the {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} years ({{ill|1661|Q7005|qid=Q7005}}-{{ill|1673|Q7617|qid=Q7617}}), a shrine was built at the current location on the orders of the founder of the Mito domain, {{ill|Tokugawa Yorifusa|Q1133680|qid=Q1133680}}, and it was said to be the guardian deity of safe childbirth. It is said that there was a tradition of borrowing a statue from the head office when giving birth, and then returning it and offering it after a safe delivery. The offspring were Chinami, Mikawa, and Kasahara. Kasahara Shrine became a religious corporation in September 1952 ({{ill|1952|Q5272|qid=Q5272}}), and is now known as ``Kasahara Yasu Shrine'' under the jurisdiction of the umbrella organization {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.
: According to the documents owned by Yoshida Shrine, on February 24, {{ill|Enkyō (Kamakura period)|Q1327068|qid=Q1327068|lt=Enkei}} 2nd year ({{ill|1309|Q5726|qid=Q5726}}), the then Saemon-jo and Uemon-jo issued a reply regarding ``Yoshida Kasahara Shrine Transfer Shrine.'' Furthermore, on May 25, 1996 ({{ill|1396|Q6405|qid=Q6405}}), Ujiyoshi Sani sent out a letter of donation stating, ``Kasahara Gosha Gotodensho Hōdonoya'' (from ``Suifu Geion Koroki'').

; Sakamon Shrine (Sakamon Daimyojin)
:* Enshrinement location: Sakamon-cho, Mito City ({{Coord|36|21|22.47|N|140|29|52.64|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Bekku: Sakamon Shrine}})
:* Enshrined deity: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konohana Sakuyahime}}

=== Precincts Suesha ===
* Rokusha (on the right side facing the main shrine)
** Matsuo Shrine - A branch of {{ill|Matsunoo Taisha|Q710302|qid=Q710302}} in {{ill|Kyōto|Q740246|qid=Q740246}}.
** Taga Shrine - A branch of {{ill|Taga-taisha|Q402091|qid=Q402091}} in {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358|lt=Shiga}}.
** Sumiyoshi Shrine - A branch of {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|qid=Q11381857}} in {{ill|Ōsaka|Q11439906|qid=Q11439906}}.
** Hachiman Shrine - A branch of {{ill|Hachiman shrine|Q11390939|qid=Q11390939}}.
** Okunishushi Daishu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Okunishushi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro no Mikoto}}.
** Small Pox Guardian Shrine

* Two shrines (back right facing the main shrine)
*: A simple shrine building built with a terraced structure. Both companies are mentioned in the ``Chinjucho'' and ``Jinhachisha Ryakuenshi.''
** Kunimi Shrine - Enshrined deity: Hikokuni Mikaki Kenyotsuka no Mikoto. {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}He is the enshrined deity of Geku Setsusha and {{ill|Watarai Kunimi Shrine|Q11486118|qid=Q11486118}}, and the ancestor of Ise Kunizo and Watarai Shinto priests.
** Hayatoshi Shrine - Enshrined deity: Ryodoirihime no Mikoto. One of the wives of Takeru of Japan and the mother of Emperor Chuai.

* Two shrines (back left facing the main shrine)
*: A simple shrine building built with a terraced structure. Both companies are mentioned in the ``Chinjucho'' and ``Jinhachisha Ryakuenshi.''
** Ii Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}. He was the second prince of Japan Takeru, and his mother was Ryodo Irihime no Mikoto.**: "Shingusha" is written in "Chinjucho". The ``Shuhachisha Ryakuenshi'' describes it as ``Ii Shrine'' and ``Kehi Myojin''.
** Mito Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hayaakitsuhiko no Mikoto}}. A branch of Mito Shrine in Kasahara-cho, Mito City.

* Two shrines (Kodaijingu Shrine and Toyouke Daijingu Shrine)
*: "Shuhachisha Ryakuenshi" says "Ise Nisho Bekku". A branch of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|lt=Naiku}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Geku}}. The shrine building is Nigensha {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545}}.
** Kodai Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu}}.
** Toyouke Daijingu Shrine - Deity enshrined: {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyouke Hime no Mikoto}}.

* Inari Shrine/Hashi Shrine
*: In "Shuhachisha Ryoenshi", it is only described as {{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari Myojin}}. A simple shrine building built with a terraced structure.

* Hoshimiya Shrine
* Tenmangu - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}
*: ``Chinjucho'' says ``Tenjin Shrine,'' and ``Shuhachisha Ryakuenshi'' says ``Tenma Tenjin.'' While all the other subsidiary shrines have small shrine buildings, Tenmangu Shrine has a medium-sized, flowing-style shrine building with a well-maintained place of worship.

*: In the old days, it was held on {{ill|September 15 (Lunisolar)|Q840070|qid=Q840070|lt=September 15th of the lunar calendar}}. A grand mikoshi crossing to the Naka River is held {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.
* Shichi-Go-San prayer (during November)
* Labor Thanksgiving Day ({{ill|November 23|Q3021|qid=Q3021}})
* Great Purification ({{ill|December 31|Q2912|qid=Q2912}})

=== Cultural assets ===
* Yoshida Shrine Documents
*: Hitachi's leading shrine document {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (National History)|1993}}. The original was destroyed in the war, but a manuscript remains in the Shokokan collection {{Sfn|Yoshida Shrine (National History)|1993}}.

'''Historical materials'''
* "Chinjucho" (included in "Shinto Taikei")
*: Shrine book under the Mito domain after the organization of shrines conducted by the Mito domain during the Kanbun and Genroku years (1661-1703). The exact year of establishment is unknown.
* "Shinhachisha Ryakuenshi" (included in "Shinto Taikei")
*: Written by Shuto Ishii. January 1797. A document that examines 28 Shikinai companies in Hitachi Province.
* “Hitachi 28 Shako” (included in “Shinto Taikei”)
*: Written by Nobutaka Aoyama. December 1799. A document that examines 28 Shikinai companies in Hitachi Province.
* “Suifu Gei-on Koroki”
*: Written by Taneaki Takakura.
